articles.summary: Musk, who will have more than 50% of the voting power, will have a monarchical grip over the publicly-traded version of SpaceX — control that goes far beyond what other tech founders enjoy.

articles.title: Law enforcement shuts down VPN service used by two dozen ransomware gangs
articles.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
articles.summary: First VPN promised hackers complete anonymity for their cyberattacks. But Europol said it was able to notify the service’s users that they have now been identified.

articles.title: Six search engines worth trying now that Google isn’t really Google anymore
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.summary: Google is about to look really different, and if you’re not a fan of the AI overview feature, then you’re not going to like what’s coming.

articles.title: Convective Capital raises an $85 million fund to build disaster resilience
articles.author: Tim Fernholz
articles.summary: After launching to invest in fire tech, Convective is broadening its mandate to disaster resilience.

articles.title: Trump delays AI security executive order, saying language ‘could have been a blocker’
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan
articles.summary: President Trump delayed signing an executive order that would have required pre-release government security reviews of AI models, citing dissatisfaction with the order’s language.

articles.title: This young startup is taking on a fragrance industry that hasn’t changed in almost half a century
articles.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
articles.summary: Fragrance tech company Patina announced Thursday a $2 million raise from investors, including Betaworks and True Ventures.

articles.title: Spotify launches an ElevenLabs-powered audiobook creation tool
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: The AI-powered audiobook generation won’t bind authors to an exclusive contract, meaning they are free to publish their generated audiobooks anywhere.

articles.title: Spotify adds AI-powered Q&A and briefing generation features to podcasts
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Spotify will let you generate daily or weekly briefs based on your prompts

articles.title: Spotify takes on Google’s NotebookLM with its new app
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Spotify is releasing the new desktop app as a research preview in more than 20 markets.

articles.title: Spotify will reserve tickets for top fans of an artists in a bid to drum up engagement
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Spotify said that it will monitor activity like streams and shares to determine who is a top fan

articles.title: Maka Kids is redefining kids’ screen time with a streaming app optimized for well-being, not engagement
articles.author: Aisha Malik
articles.summary: Maka Kids is building a streaming app for children ages zero to six featuring content designed for healthy development. The startup has now raised $3 million in seed funding to scale its platform.

articles.title: Hark raises $700M Series A for its secretive ‘universal’ AI interface
articles.author: Tim Fernholz
articles.summary: Hark expects to release its first multimodal models this summer, which it says will power a personal AI platform that works with existing products and services. The company expects to follow that with hardware devices built specifically for those systems.

articles.title: The Path, founded by Tony Robbins and Calm alums, hopes to offer safer AI therapy
articles.author: Julie Bort
articles.summary: The Path says its AI model has scored 95 on the mental health safety AI benchmark, Vera-MH. This compares to a top score of 65 for the consumer bots.

articles.title: Google is pitching an AI agent ecosystem to consumers who may not buy it
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.summary: One of the most promising introductions at Google’s I/O developer conference on Tuesday was a new way for consumers to use the web: AI agents. Unfortunately, it was also the most confusing.

articles.title: Wayve’s self-driving tech is headed to US cars made by Stellantis
articles.author: Kirsten Korosec
articles.summary: Wayve’s self-driving tech will show up in Stellantis vehicles in 2028.

articles.title: With aluminum prices up 20%, recycling startups bet on AI to cash in
articles.author: Tim De Chant
articles.summary: Recycling startups are using AI to improve the recovery of critical minerals like aluminum, aiming to build a massive source of the metal.

articles.title: Flipper unveils a Linux-powered networking gadget built for hackers and tinkerers
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Flipper Devices said that the new gadget is in development and the base model will cost under $350.

articles.title: Scammers are abusing an internal Microsoft account to send spam links
articles.author: Zack Whittaker
articles.summary: The loophole allows spammers and scammers to send emails from a legitimate Microsoft email address typically used for sending genuine account alerts.

articles.title: Beauty booking startup Fresha hits $1B valuation with KKR backing
articles.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
articles.summary: Beauty and wellness booking marketplace Fresha says it has raised $80 million investment from KKR’s Next Generation Technology Growth fund, KKR’s growth equity arm.

articles.title: Truecaller gets into the eSIM business to diversify its revenue streams
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: The company said its plans will range from 1 GB over 7 days to 20 GB over 30 days. Initially, the launch will make the eSIM product available in 29 countries.

articles.title: General Catalyst just led a $63M bet on India’s travel payments market
articles.author: Jagmeet Singh
articles.summary: Scapia, an Indian startup that combines travel booking with co-branded credit cards and mobile payments, said the deal doubles its valuation.

articles.title: Imperagen raises £5 million to use quantum physics, AI on enzyme engineering
articles.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
articles.summary: Biotech company Imperagen announced on Thursday a £5 million ($6.7 million) seed round led by PXN Ventures, with participation from IQ Capital and Northern Gritstone.

articles.title: Jensen Huang says he’s found a ‘brand new’ $200B market for Nvidia
articles.author: Julie Bort
articles.summary: The next big thing for Nvidia will be CPUs for AI agents, $200 billion worth, CEO Jensen Huang predicts.

articles.title: Anthropic says it’s about to have its first profitable quarter
articles.author: Lucas Ropek
articles.summary: Anthropic has told its investors that it will more than double revenue to around $10.9 billion in its second quarter.

articles.title: The SpaceX IPO filing is filled with AI bets, Starship dreams, and Elon Musk at the center
articles.author: Sean O'Kane, Kirsten Korosec
articles.summary: SpaceX has finally made the contents of its IPO filing public, weeks ahead of what is expected to be the largest IPO ever and one that will make Musk the CEO, CTO, and chairman of the board.

articles.title: Clouted wants to take the guesswork out of making short videos go viral
articles.author: Marina Temkin
articles.summary: The video clipping startup raised a $7 million seed round led by Slow Ventures.

articles.title: xAI burned $6.4B last year — SpaceX’s IPO filing shows why the spending is far from over
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan
articles.summary: SpaceX’s IPO filing reveals xAI lost $6.4 billion in 2025 while planning a massive Grok expansion — offering the first public look at Elon Musk’s AI financials and more details about his ambitions.

articles.title: Nvidia posts another record quarter, reveals $43B of holdings in startups
articles.author: Russell Brandom
articles.summary: Nvidia announced another record revenue figure after market close on Wednesday, but forecasted that revenue growth would slow in the following quarter.

articles.title: Musk’s xAI is being sued over its data center generators — now it’s buying $2.8B more
articles.author: Tim De Chant
articles.summary: Elon Musk’s xAI said it will buy $2.8 billion worth of natural gas turbines over the next three years, according to SpaceX’s IPO filing.

articles.title: Anthropic will pay xAI $1.25B per month for compute
articles.author: Tim De Chant
articles.summary: Elon Musk’s xAI surprised the AI world when it made a deal to sell compute to Anthropic. Now we know how much it’s worth.

articles.title: Sam Altman makes ‘mic drop’ offer to every Y Combinator startup
articles.author: Julie Bort
articles.summary: Altman offered to have OpenAI invest in every single startup in this Y Combinator class: tokens for equity.

articles.title: Microsoft’s carbon-removal plans aren’t dead after all
articles.author: Tim De Chant
articles.summary: Microsoft is responsible for over 90% of the carbon-removal market, and reports suggested the company was pausing purchases entirely. This new deal should help assuage the fears of CDR startups.

articles.title: OpenAI claims it solved an 80-year-old math problem — for real this time
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan
articles.summary: OpenAI claims its reasoning model disproved a geometry conjecture unsolved since 1946 — and this time, the mathematicians who exposed its last embarrassing claim are backing it up.

articles.title: IrisGo, a startup backed by Andrew Ng, looks to become the AI desktop buddy you never knew you needed
articles.author: Lucas Ropek
articles.summary: Initially billed as an “AI butler,” Iris watches what happens on a user’s desktop and automatically learns how to do tasks for them, its co-founder says.

articles.title: Tesla’s Full Self-Driving software is creeping into Europe
articles.author: Kirsten Korosec
articles.summary: First came the Netherlands, now it’s Lithuania. And more European countries appear to be in the queue for Tesla’s driver-assistance system.

articles.title: Airbnb gets into hotels, expands AI for host onboarding and customer support
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Airbnb will soon let you book luggage storage and car rental services on its app.

articles.title: Global EV market goes K-shaped as the US gets left behind
articles.author: Tim De Chant
articles.summary: EV sales have surged worldwide in every region but the U.S., posing risks for legacy and startup automakers.

articles.title: OpenAI barrels toward IPO that may happen in September
articles.author: Julie Bort
articles.summary: A day after Elon Musk lost his lawsuit that threatened OpenAI’s structure, leadership, and finances, OpenAI is reportedly back to prepping for its IPO.

articles.title: Jeff Bezos, you were so close to making a good point
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.summary: “Why is a nurse in Queens who makes $75,000 a year paying more than $1,000 a month in taxes?” Bezos said Wednesday morning on CNBC. “That’s $1,000 that could help with rent, or groceries, or anything.”

articles.title: Customers say Trump Mobile is leaking their personal information
articles.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
articles.summary: Trump Mobile is leaking customers’ email and home addresses but has not responded to people alerting the company of the data exposure, according to two YouTubers who said they verified that their leaked data is authentic.

articles.title: Intuit to lay off over 3,000 employees to refocus on AI
articles.author: Ram Iyer
articles.summary: In a memo to employees, CEO Sasan Goodarzi said the layoffs are meant to reduce complexity, simplify the company’s corporate structure, and deliver better AI products.

articles.title: AI search startups are blowing up
articles.author: Russell Brandom
articles.summary: AI search has quietly become one of the most attractive targets in consumer AI.

articles.title: Stability AI releases a new audio model that can create 6-minute songs
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Stability Audio 3.0 small model can run on-device and generate two-minute long tracks.

articles.title: Startup Battlefield 200 applications close in 1 week: Window to nominate and apply for the most promising startups closes May 27
articles.author: TechCrunch Events
articles.summary: Startup Battlefield 200 applications close May 27. Pitch at TechCrunch Disrupt, get investor access, win $100K, plus more scaling perks. Nominate an early-stage founder or submit your startup today.

articles.title: NanoClaw creator turns down $20M buyout offer, raises $12M seed instead
articles.author: Julie Bort
articles.summary: NanoClaw was created as a secure alternative to OpenClaw to assist the Cohen brothers with their AI marketing firm that used agents to do much of the work. But instead of running directly on a computer, NanoClaw runs sandboxed in a container.

articles.title: GitHub says hackers stole data from thousands of internal repositories
articles.author: Zack Whittaker
articles.summary: The code hosting giant GitHub said it was investigating a breach but said there was no evidence of customer data theft.

articles.title: This startup raised $43M to build a hive mind for ships
articles.author: Sean O'Kane
articles.summary: The Arlington, Virginia-based startup has raised $42 million to equip ships with sensors that blow the current AIS tech out of the water.

articles.title: Figma adds an AI assistant to its collaborative canvas
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Figma says users can employ natural language text prompts to direct its new AI agent to generate new designs, edit existing ones, or automate tasks such as generating iterations of existing designs.

articles.title: ‘Ask YouTube’ brings AI-powered conversational search to video, adds Gemini Omni to Shorts
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.summary: Google is completely revamping its search experience, and that doesn’t stop at YouTube.

articles.title: Google just declared itself a contender in AI design at IO 2026
articles.author: Aisha Malik
articles.summary: Google says it’s designed the app to be accessible to everyone, from teachers to small business owners.

articles.title: You can now talk to your Gmail inbox, as seen at Google IO 2026
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.summary: Google expands Gmail’s AI Inbox with conversational voice search, letting users ask Gemini to find buried email details.

articles.title: How to use Google’s new AI agents to go beyond your standard searches
articles.author: Lauren Forristal
articles.summary: Google is launching AI-powered “information agents” that can monitor topics in the background and proactively alert users to updates and changes.

articles.title: Discord enables end-to-end encrypted voice and video calling for every user
articles.author: Zack Whittaker
articles.summary: Good news! Discord’s hundreds of millions of users now have their communications scrambled, so not even Discord can see them.

articles.title: Mach Industries just spent $50M to solve a major defense tech problem
articles.author: Connie Loizos
articles.summary: Mach says the acquisition meaningfully improves unit economics across its five vehicle programs at exactly the moment the company is starting to scale.

articles.title: From teen hacker to Iron Dome researcher, this founder raised $28M to fight AI phishing
articles.author: Marina Temkin
articles.summary: Ocean, an agentic email security platform, claims its AI can thoroughly analyze the context of every incoming email to detect fraud and impersonation attempts.

articles.title: Elon Musk said Sam Altman ‘stole’ a non-profit — but the trial showed he had similar aims
articles.author: Tim Fernholz
articles.summary: The jury’s speedy decision to reject Elon Musk’s lawsuit against the other founders of OpenAI and Microsoft confirmed what we saw in the courtroom: Musk’s case was a weak one, in part because he waited so long to file it.

articles.title: Google takes a page out of Meta’s book, announces new audio-powered smart glasses at IO 2026
articles.author: Lucas Ropek
articles.summary: Google is calling the new devices “audio glasses,” in that users will be able to issue verbal commands to them and get things done via its ecosystem of apps and services, including Gemini.

articles.title: Google’s Genie world model can now simulate real streets with Street View
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan
articles.summary: Google DeepMind is integrating Street View with Project Genie to create immersive, interactive world simulations for robotics, gaming, and travel, allowing users to explore environments, weather changes, and rare scenarios.

articles.title: With Gemini 3.5 Flash, Google bets its next AI wave on agents, not chatbots
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan
articles.summary: Google launched Gemini 3.5 Flash, its most powerful coding and agentic AI model yet, at the company’s annual developer conference. It is capable of autonomously executing complex tasks and building software from scratch.

articles.title: Google Search as you know it is over
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.summary: Google is transforming Search from a list of links into an AI-powered experience filled with conversational answers, autonomous agents, and interactive interfaces — a shift that could further reduce traffic to publishers across the web.

articles.title: OpenAI is making it easier to check if an image was made by their models
articles.author: Russell Brandom
articles.summary: OpenAI announced two new measures to help detect AI generated imagery: joining the open C2PA standard and adding Google’s SynthID to its products.

articles.title: Google’s Gemini Omni turns images, audio, and text into video — and that’s just the start
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan
articles.summary: Google’s Gemini Omni is a new multimodal model that reasons across text, images, audio, and video to generate and edit videos through simple conversation — starting with Omni Flash.

articles.title: Google launches Antigravity 2.0 with an updated desktop app and CLI tool at IO 2026
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Google is debuting a new AI Ultra plan priced at $100, which will give users 5x more usage limit than the AI Pro plan alongside the Antigravity 2.0 launch.

articles.title: Google adds voice-based prompting to Docs and Keep
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Google is letting users create drafts, take notes, and search for email with voice with the new Workspace update.

articles.title: Google introduces Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agentic assistant with Gmail integration, at IO 2026
articles.author: Russell Brandom
articles.summary: At the Google I/O developer conference, the company announced a new agentic personal assistant called Gemini Spark, built from Gemini’s base models and an agentic harness from Google Antigravity.

articles.title: Google’s new Universal Cart wants to follow your entire shopping journey across the internet
articles.author: Aisha Malik
articles.summary: Most people shop across multiple devices, many retailers, and over the course of many days, which is why Google is launching Universal Cart.

articles.title: Agentic app coding gets an upgrade with Google’s release of Android CLI
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.summary: Google is embracing the rise of AI coding agents with new Android tools designed to work with platforms like Claude Code and OpenAI’s Codex, allowing developers — or their AI assistants — to build Android apps faster from the command line.

articles.title: Google updates its Gemini app to take on ChatGPT and Claude at IO 2026
articles.author: Aisha Malik
articles.summary: The updates signal Google’s push to turn its Gemini app into an all-purpose AI hub rather than a stand-alone chatbot.

articles.title: Google’s AI Studio now lets anyone build Android apps in minutes
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.summary: Google unveiled new web-based AI tools that can generate native Android apps in minutes, as the company expands its push into AI-powered software development.

articles.title: OpenAI co-founder Andrej Karpathy joins Anthropic’s pre-training team
articles.author: Rebecca Bellan, Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
articles.summary: Pre-training is responsible for the large-scale training runs that give Claude its core knowledge and capabilities, according to the company. It’s also one of the most expensive, compute-intensive phases of building a frontier model.

articles.title: The minimalist Light Phone teams up with Andrew Yang’s Noble Mobile, which pays you to stop doomscrolling
articles.author: Amanda Silberling
articles.summary: “The Light Phone is designed to be used as little as possible,” founder Joe Hollier told TechCrunch.

articles.title: Hackers have compromised dozens of popular open source packages in an ongoing supply-chain attack
articles.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
articles.summary: The attacks are part of a wider campaign known as Mini Shai-Hulud, which has already compromised several open source projects and, in turn, developers and companies that use them.

articles.title: US cyber agency CISA exposed reams of passwords and cloud keys to the open web
articles.author: Zack Whittaker
articles.summary: The federal cybersecurity agency left plaintext passwords in a spreadsheet uploaded to a public GitHub repository, per a report by independent journalist Brian Krebs.

articles.title: Apple announces Apple Intelligence-powered accessibility feature updates
articles.author: Ivan Mehta
articles.summary: Apple announced several new accessibility updates to features like VoiceOver, voice control, live recognition, and real-time caption generation for videos that will be powered by Apple Intelligence.

articles.title: Forget the feed: Status AI raises $17M to turn social media into interactive entertainment
articles.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
articles.summary: “Status is built on the premise that the next generation doesn’t want to watch stories,” CEO and co-founder Fai Nur said. “They want to engage with the stories and even live inside them.”

articles.title: ‘Survivor’ stars Kyle Fraser and Kamilla Karthigesu introduce a goal-tracking app, Paprclip
articles.author: Sarah Perez
articles.summary: A new app from “Survivor” season 48 winner Kyle Fraser and castmate Kamilla Karthigesu aims to turn goal tracking into a social experience, pairing users for accountability, daily challenges, and shared progress clips.

articles.title: Stilta raises $10.5M from a16z and YC to help companies rediscover the patents they forgot they had
articles.author: Dominic-Madori Davis
articles.summary: Stilta is an AI platform designed to automate the research and analytical work behind intellectual property cases — the kind of labor-intensive work that has historically made patent litigation slow and expensive.

articles.title: Solar to dominate energy by 2035, but AI data centers will keep fossil fuels in business
articles.author: Tim De Chant
articles.summary: Costs for solar panels are expected to drop another 30% in the coming decade, helping the tech cement its lead in energy markets.

articles.title: Theo Baker spent four years investigating Stanford. Before he leaves, here’s what he found.
articles.author: Connie Loizos
articles.summary: “There’s a common refrain among [young] people in this world that it’s easier to raise money for a startup right now than to get an internship. Which is remarkable, right?”

articles.title: OSHA probing worker death at SpaceX’s Starbase site
articles.author: Sean O'Kane
articles.summary: The death is the latest worker safety issue at the Starbase facility, which has a higher injury rate than all other SpaceX sites.

articles.title: SandboxAQ brings its drug discovery models to Claude — no PhD in computing required
articles.author: Lucas Ropek
articles.summary: Other venture-backed companies like Chai Discovery and Isomorphic Labs have raced to build better models. SandboxAQ is betting that access is the bigger obstacle and that Claude solves it.

articles.title: Anthropic has acquired the dev tools startup used by OpenAI, Google, and Cloudflare
articles.author: Kirsten Korosec
articles.summary: Stainless, a New York-based startup, founded in 2022, rose to prominence in the emerging AI industry for automating the creation and maintenance of software development kits, or SDKs — the libraries developers use to interact with APIs.

articles.title: Elon Musk has lost his lawsuit against Sam Altman and OpenAI
articles.author: Tim Fernholz
articles.summary: Elon Musk’s claim that he was mistreated by his OpenAI co-founders failed after nine California jurors decided in a unanimous verdict that his lawsuits had been filed too late.
